source_quality.notes: page 8 lost from the text layer; equations read from the raster

task_reconstruction: Quantify the effect of the Francis Scott Key Bridge collapse, choose a bus project, propose a rail project, and address safety.

section_map.summary: summary of the three models and the safety note
background and restatement of the four problems
the rerouting of the collapsed bridge

contributions.summary: edge weights from the entropy of flow, capacity and peak time
the collapsed bridge's flow moved onto the two bridges above it
five clusters of stops, each with a minimum spanning tree
one proposed north-south rail line where the overlap is weakest

dependency_graph.relation: the edge weights feed the shortest paths
the road network carries the stops
the bus network is what the rail network is compared with

assumptions.summary: travel behaviour stays fixed in the short term
road capacity stays fixed during the analysis
safety risk is proportional to the peak hour and the speed

data_and_preprocessing.summary: nodes and edges read from two files, 565496 edges
missing ridership filled by linear interpolation
outliers removed by the interquartile rule
ridership and position scaled to the unit interval

models.summary: entropy-weighted directed graph of the road network
flow balance and shortest paths after the collapse
bus stop scoring, five clusters and minimum spanning trees
bus and rail overlap with one proposed line

verification.summary: recorded bridge traffic from 2014 to 2022 drawn for both scenarios
shelter score checked against route count by a heatmap
one structural perturbation of the minimum spanning tree

results_trace.summary: flow falls near the collapsed bridge and rises near the other two
commuting time rises for urban and suburban commuters
three benefits claimed for the new line, none numbered

writing_logic.summary: the summary gives one paragraph to each model
each assumption is paired with a justification
each result is followed by the stakeholder it touches
the conclusion revisits the models in order and then the flaws

language_observations.summary: opens on a linchpin metaphor and an aim clause
a considering-phrase lists the reasons before the rerouting decision
the benefits are numbered firstly, secondly, thirdly, then a however
the memorandum pairs a benefit with a cost for each project

visualization_observations.summary: Figure 4 shades the roads by entropy weight
Figures 5 and 6 compare the flow before and after the collapse
Figure 11 ranks the stops by score and place
Figure 27 shows the overlap and marks the proposed line

judge_relevance_hypotheses.summary: tying each result to a named stakeholder matches a stakeholder brief
owning the flawed assumptions reads as honest rather than weak

weaknesses.summary: the score weights are stated with no derivation
the sensitivity claim rests on one comparison
three assumptions are owned as unrealistic and not tested
transfers and buildability are left out

independent_extensions.summary: weight the edges of a city graph by the entropy of a few factors
study a lost link by splitting its flow over the surviving links

unresolved_questions: the score weights of 0.6, 0.4 and 0.2 are never derived
the flow split is described as proportional to capacity but no formula is printed
the choice of five clusters is not justified
the sensitivity verdict rests on a single longer tree
